newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 25.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
** The U.S. Federal Reserve on Tuesday left interest rates unchanged at policy meeting

** First half profits of top Indian firms which make up the benchmark Bombay stocks index will see a sharp slowdown, but strong results from banking and auto firms are likely to soften the blow, a Reuters poll found on Tuesday
The poll of 14 leading securities houses projected an average 20.6 percent rise in the net profit of 30 index firms during the first half ended September 30, 1996 from around 40 percent a year ago.

Net sales growth was pegged at a modest 16.5 percent. ** Industry secretary N. Mohanty says the government would soon come out with fresh criteria for 100 percent foreign investments, the Business Standard reports
** Slowing economy has hit export with the growth halving to 10 percent, Commerce secretary says, the Economic Times reports
** The spot dollar/rupee INR= opened little changed at 35.67/68 per dollar and seen gaining, dealers say
** On Tuesday, selective buying by foreign institutional investors pulled Indian shares to positive territory at close but undercurrent was suspect, traders said
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 6.64 points, or 0.20 percent, lower at 3,337.73
** The 100-share National index added 2.06 points, or 0.14 percent, at 1,491.06
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index gained 0.07 points to 968.91
** The 500-share CRISIL index was off 1.07 points, or 0.16 percent, at 650.56
** The Delhi share index gained 2.62 points to 739.13
** The Calcutta index rose 1.44 points to 430.27
** The Madras index firmed 1.89 points to 3,418.69
** The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index slipped 0.12 points, or 0.17 percent, to 68.66 with the premium over the local market at 12.84 percent
